Gel des permis de travail temporaire: fa: Temporary work permit freeze: is there really cause for concern?
Les travailleurs étrangers ont 4 jours p: Foreign workers have four days to renew or obtain a closed work permit before new TFWP restrictions take effect in Montréal.
<strong>Détenteurs de permis de travail: Whether they hold “closed” work permits or are looking for a job, foreign workers have only four days left to renew or obtain the precious document in Montréal, or risk having their future application refused. For the other provinces, the deadline is September 26. For La Converse, a lawyer breaks down these political decisions that caught everyone off guard.
Le 20 août 2024, le premier ministre du: On August 20, 2024, Quebec Premier François Legault announced a partial suspension of the Temporary Foreign Worker Program (TFWP) for six months, starting September 3, 2024. The following week, it was Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's turn to announce federal measures to reduce the number of temporary foreign workers in low-wage jobs, set to take effect on September 26.
Le PTET permet aux entreprises d’embauch: The TFWP allows businesses to hire foreign nationals to fill positions for which they face a labour shortage. These employees receive what is known as a “closed” work permit, meaning one that authorizes them to work for a single employer only. If they lose their job, their work permit is no longer valid. The system is regularly questioned and criticized by those who believe it places these workers in a precarious position. With these surprise announcements, the Quebec and federal governments appear to be putting up new obstacles, citing inflation and the <l1>housing crisis</l1> to justify them.
Concrètement, du 3 septembre 2024 au 3 m: In concrete terms, from September 3, 2024 to March 3, 2025, Montréal employers will no longer be able to submit hiring applications under the TFWP for positions below the median wage of CAN$57,000 gross per year. Starting September 26, several similar federal measures will apply to provinces with an unemployment rate above 6%. The government is conducting a review of the program and has not given an end date for this measure for the time being.
« Si ma demande est rejetée, je vais dev: “If my application is rejected, I'll have to go back to Colombia”
Dans les bureaux du Centre d’aide aux fa: In the offices of the Centre d'aide aux familles latino-américaines (CAFLA), an organization that provides health support to closed work permit holders, Malia*, a volunteer for six months, agreed to open up to La Converse. Originally from Colombia, she arrived in Montréal last March on a visitor visa. “I came to be close to my children. My son and my daughter have been studying here for 3 years. My daughter is 17 and still in high school, so she needed my help with all the administrative steps,” she explains.
Psychologue spécialisée dans la petite e: A psychologist specializing in early childhood for 20 years in Colombia, Malia seized the opportunity of her stay to put her expertise at the service of the Latina community by volunteering for CAFLA. With her visitor visa set to expire on September 21, Malia finds herself in total confusion. CAFLA offered her a position as a psychologist, but her contract stipulates a salary below the $57,000 per year threshold, which would exempt her from the latest immigration measures. “Even though I was offered a job here, we are a community organization… I won't be paid more than $27.47 per hour. If my application is rejected, I'll have to go back to Colombia,” she says with a sigh.
En théorie, Malia ayant déjà présenté sa: In theory, since Malia has already submitted her application for a “closed” permit, she should slip through the net. That isn't enough to ease her stress, however. “It's a very difficult situation. This morning again I was about to cry. It's very hard, the noose is tightening,” she says with emotion.
Ces annonces ont provoqué un « choc et u: These announcements caused “shock and panic” among foreign workers with precarious status, says Cecilia Ivonne Escamilla, director of the Centre d'aide aux familles latino-américaines (CAFLA), an organization that provides health support to closed work permit holders. On social media, some Facebook groups of foreign workers are also buzzing. “Urgent: I've had my temporary foreign worker permit for 8 months, does this news affect me?” reads a post in one of these groups.
Mais ces personnes ont-elles raison de s: But are these people right to worry? La Converse put the question to a lawyer.
« Plusieurs domaines d’emploi ne seront: “Several fields of employment won't be affected”
Au-delà des mesures générales, certains: Beyond the general measures, some details need to be taken into account. “Very few people will be affected, because under these criteria, several fields of employment won't be touched. Workers in health, education, construction, food processing and agriculture are exempt, for example,” says Stéphane Handfield, a Montréal-based immigration lawyer. Indeed, the measures mainly target employees in retail, hospitality and food service.
L’expert rappelle par ailleurs que les n: The expert also points out that the new TFWP rules in Quebec apply only to the island of Montréal: “Someone who lives in Montréal and finds a job in Laval, Joliette or elsewhere will have no problem,” explains Handfield. It is the place of employment that counts, not the place of residence.
Bien qu’Ottawa ait également annoncé des: Although Ottawa has also announced similar measures for the rest of the country, starting September 26, the immigration lawyer stresses that they apply only to provinces with an unemployment rate above 6%. “If you look, for example, at the greater Quebec City metropolitan area, the unemployment rate is below 6%, so the measure won't apply to that region. There will be a lot of exceptions,” he insists.
Cependant, les mesures fédérales réduise: However, the federal measures also lower the maximum share of TFWP workers per company. The percentage of low-wage foreign employees that an employer is allowed to hire will drop from 20% to 10% of the total workforce. In addition, the maximum duration of these work permits will be reduced to one year instead of two. The opportunity to obtain permanent residency after two years of employment in Canada will therefore be out of reach if a work permit renewal is refused. “Reducing the length of the work permit from two years to one, yes, that can cause problems for getting permanent residency. But depending on the type of job, many people already don't have access to it,” Handfield continues.
L’avocat met en lumière certains aspects: The lawyer highlights certain aspects of Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's announcements that he considers “contradictory.” “The federal government announced this measure for September 26, but at the same time we see Immigration Canada speeding up the processing of work permit applications in order to finalize as many files as possible before the measures take effect,” he analyzes.
« On met des mesures pour restreindre le: “Measures are being put in place to restrict the numbers, but at the same time, in the days before they take effect, files are being processed faster. So it's not impossible that changes will be made to how permanent residency is obtained,” according to the immigration lawyer. Hardly reassuring for those affected. Especially since the fear of having to leave the country could lead to abuses.
De retour au CAFLA, la directrice Cecili: Back at CAFLA, director Cecilia Ivonne Escamilla welcomes us into her office, right next to Malia's. “With these new measures, qualified professionals will be forced to accept any job just to be able to stay here. The situation is likely to get worse, because these workers, out of fear of losing their status, won't demand their rights and will do whatever they're told. That makes the situation even more precarious for these people,” she explains.
Dans son <l1>rapport présenté au Conseil: In his <l1>report presented to the United Nations Human Rights Council on July 22, 2024</l1>, rapporteur Tomoya Obokata is not gentle with Canada. On the TFWP, he says closed permits are “a breeding ground for contemporary forms of slavery” and that “The government does not appear to proactively and effectively inform workers of their rights.”
« Pour moi, ça s’apparente bien à de l’e: “To me, it's very much akin to slavery,” says Cecilia Ivonne Escamilla. She particularly objects to the power imbalance that develops between an employer and their employee: “For a temporary worker to be able to come back the following year, they must obtain a document certifying that they are authorized to do so. Without that document, they can't return. If they complain or cause problems, they risk not getting that paper from their employer and being barred from returning. They pay taxes and have rights, but they keep quiet, because they fear having to go back to their country.”
La directrice craint également que de no: The director also fears that many workers will remain in Canada <l1>without status</l1> if their permits are not renewed, which would further complicate their situation. “When they go from having a work permit to being undocumented, they'll just end up working under the table and employers take advantage of it, it's terrible,” she laments.
Alors que le compte à rebours est lancé,: As the countdown begins, the question of the consequences of the latest immigration policies for workers looms large. La Converse will continue to follow this situation, because beyond the numbers and the political decisions, human lives are at stake.
